name: Real apply body honours gates and clamps
non_visual_rationale: A pure function's verdict inside the scoring engine. Nothing renders: build.ts still hands applyCorrection a literal null, so no published byte can move on this step at all. The observables are a returned gate token, a score delta and a member-height bias. U1-U8 and a Vera walk are N/A.
criteria_delivered: 1. applyCorrection(seed, record) re-checks n >= 10, reporters >= 5, abs(b) > 2*se from the record's OWN stated fields before applying anything. The stored `applied` boolean is never read; gateCorrection is imported from src/learning/gates.ts rather than restated, so apply and fit cannot drift apart and both anti-Sybil amendments are inherited with no new inputs.

2. applyCorrection(seed, null) still returns gate no_file, zero delta_q, zero member bias. tests/unit/scoring-laws.test.ts is byte-identical through this step and its R19 no-file identity law stays green as an independent fence.

3. PARTIAL, by design, see criteria_deferred. The first half ships: a member is corrected by the difference stored at its OWN (source, lead bucket) key, and by exactly zero at a key the record does not state. The 0.40-of-member-height clamp does NOT ship.
4. delta_q is MINUS the record's score b over 100, saturated at the record's own clamp.max_abs_score (12 display points as the emitter writes it). 06 section 4's sign, not 05 section 5's stale line.
5. combine keeps arity 3; no new parameter reaches the score path. Shipped scoring-laws R20 (combine.length === 3) stays green unchanged.
criteria_deferred: 3 (second half). 'clamped to 0.40 of the member height' cannot bind here. 05 section 5 pins the port at memberHBias(source, lead_h): two arguments, no height. The only production call site that knows a member's own height is src/pipeline/build.ts line 218, and this lane is under a standing instruction not to touch that file while a concurrent lane (f-see-what-killed-it phase 05, worktree /Users/andres/psb-deltas-slice0405) is actively modifying it. Widening memberHBias to take the height was considered and rejected: a required third parameter breaks build.ts's compile, and an optional one has no honest default (defaulting to unclamped hands the next step a silently unclamped height; defaulting to zero makes the whole lane inert behind a signature that claims otherwise). The clamp therefore lands with 02-05's height half, together with the one build.ts edit that feeds it the height. FLAGGED: between 02-03's wiring and 02-05's clamp, a member height moves unclamped. That window is inside this feature branch, is bounded by 02-05's own acceptance scenario, and no published byte moves until 02-03 lands.
files_untouched_deliberately: src/pipeline/build.ts -- owned by a concurrent lane; git diff over this step names only the four paths above.
tests/unit/scoring-laws.test.ts -- the feature-delta Test Reuse table marks its correction laws PRESERVE, and they are this step's independent fence. Byte-identical.
harness_note: The accepted roadmap points this step at cucumber scenarios in a-correction-file-can-never-move-a-number-past-the-gates.feature and at a PENDING_SLICES entry. Neither exists on this branch; both live on recover/learning-build. Every committed acceptance step of this feature here proves its claim with one Vitest acceptance file, 1:1, and this step follows that shape. There was no skip marker to delete. The Vitest file's oracles were checked line by line against the authored .feature on recover/learning-build (git show f07943d:...): both forged scenarios there assert 'the waves AND score a surfer reads are exactly what day zero published', which is the whole-record verdict the oracles here encode.
acceptance: Four named examples through applyCorrection. (1) A record forged to claim it was applied on six mornings is stopped and the outcome names n_lt_10. (2) A record forged to claim it was applied whose score difference is buried in its own stated error (se rewritten to 100) is stopped and names not_significant. (3) A record whose own stated evidence clears every rung moves the score by MINUS b/100 and corrects the member by the metres stored at its own model and lead bucket. (4) No file at all still returns no_file, zero, zero. Three of the four oracles reject a controlled doctored outcome of their own. Every fixture is what buildCorrectionRecords actually emits for the stated mornings and people, not a hand-typed literal, so the claims are measured against the writer on the other side of the file.
unit_law: Four fast-check laws over generated records (200-300 runs each), with each key's stored `applied` boolean generated INDEPENDENTLY of the evidence beside it, which is exactly the shape a forged or stale file has. (a) A record claiming every key was applied and the same record claiming none produce byte-identical outcomes -- gate, score delta and every member bias. (b) No number moves unless the stated evidence behind that very number cleared the ladder. (c) The score move is MINUS the stored difference over 100 and never passes the limit the record itself states; max_abs_score is GENERATED rather than pinned to the shipped constant, so a body that hardcoded 12 is caught. (d) A member is corrected by the metres at its own key and by exactly zero at a key no record states. Plus one pinned example: a stored thirty-point move reaches the published score as twelve points.
design_decision_one_file_one_verdict: The score key is the record's verdict. It is the key a forged file moves a published score with, build.ts archives exactly one bias_gate per call, and the authored .feature says a refused file leaves 'the waves AND score' at day zero. So a file the score ladder refuses moves nothing at all, height included. Past that gate each member is still corrected only if its OWN key clears the ladder too, so one thinly-sampled lead bucket costs its own bucket rather than the whole file -- an every-key-must-pass rule would make the layer inert in production, where a rarely-observed lead bucket almost always sits under ten mornings. A record stating no score move at all states no evidence this body can weigh and is refused on the first rung, like any other file with too few mornings behind it.
declarations_trap: applyCorrection must name the gate that stopped a file, but src/learning/declarations.ts's whole-source examination flags the string literal 'applied' in any value position outside a file whose basename starts with `gates`. The token is therefore CARRIED: GateVerdict.reason was narrowed from `string` to a GateReason union in gates.ts (a type-only change, inside a type span, in the one privileged module) and engine.ts assigns `gate: verdict.reason`. No cast, no literal. tests/unit/learning-declarations.test.ts stays green and its whole-source examination reports zero violations over the shipped src/.
red_evidence: Two observations, both semantic, zero collection errors. Acceptance: with the shipped inert stub in place, 3 of the 4 examples failed on real AssertionErrors -- 'the apply body must name the gate that stopped the file ... it said no_file' (expected n_lt_10), the same for not_significant, and 'a record that clears every gate on its own stated evidence must be applied' (expected applied). The fourth, the no-file launch identity, passed against the stub and is the preserved fence rather than a driven behaviour. Unit: 2 of the 4 laws failed with shrunk counterexamples -- 'a stored difference of 4.419417382415922 display points must move the score by -0.01 ... it moved 0' and 'ecmwf_wam at lead_24_48 must be corrected by the metres stored at its OWN key (-0.12828539611796372)'. The other two are one-directional safety laws that an inert stub satisfies by moving nothing; they acquire their force only once the body moves numbers, which is why the acceptance examples and not those two laws are what drove GREEN. Typecheck was clean at RED, so the red was behavioural and not a compile artefact.
falsifiability_evidence: Three controlled mutations of the shipped body, each reverted. (1) The ladder re-check was replaced by trusting the record's own flag (`if (!verdict.applied)` -> `if (!(correction.score_delta?.applied ?? false))`): 5 tests failed semantically, including both forged acceptance examples on 'a file the gates refused must move the score by exactly zero, whatever the file claims about itself' and the no-power law on 'a record that claims every key was applied and the same record claiming none was must produce byte-identical outcomes'. (2) The score sign was flipped (`-clamp(...)` -> `clamp(...)`): 3 tests failed, including 'the score delta must be MINUS the stored score difference over 100 (06 section 4); the stored difference was 11.999999999999995 and the delta was 0.11999999999999994'. (3) The record's own score clamp was dropped from the arithmetic: 2 tests failed, including 'the score move (0.04109974682633934) must never pass the limit the record itself states (0.01)'. After all three reverts, `git diff --stat src/` names only src/learning/gates.ts and src/scoring/engine.ts, and the full suite is green.
test_bug_fixed_in_red: The acceptance file was authored before this session and left uncommitted; it called `outcome.memberHBias(SOURCE, LEAD_H, MEMBER_HEIGHT_M)` with three arguments against the two-argument port 05 section 5 declares. `tsc --noEmit` failed it with TS2554 (vitest never would have: esbuild does not typecheck). The third argument was unused by every assertion in the file. It was removed rather than widening the shipped signature, for the reason recorded under criteria_deferred. No assertion was weakened. One assertion was ADDED: the third example now guards against a vacuous pass by asserting the fixture's height key really does clear the ladder on its own stated evidence before asserting that the number moved.
fixture_arithmetic: Measured, not assumed. Every observation in the fixture carries the same quality and the same shown score, so the sample standard error collapses to zero and the gate error is the physical floor alone. At 18 paired mornings from 6 people the emitter writes score_delta {b: 12.0, se: 2.946, n: 18, reporters: 6} -- |b| clears 2*se by better than twice over -- and a height key {b: 0.60, se: 0.0566, n: 18, reporters: 6}. Both clear every rung, so the passing example is not vacuous in either lane. At 6 mornings both keys refuse at n_lt_10, which is what the first forged example needs. The 30-point clamp example pins n: 30 deliberately: the G3 arithmetic is tight enough that a smaller sample count leaves a stored difference sitting close to twice its own floored error.
test_budget: Three new behaviours in this step (the ladder is re-run from stated evidence; the score move's sign and its saturation; per-key height lookup). No-file identity and combine arity are pre-existing behaviours already fenced by shipped scoring-laws R19 and R20 and are not re-tested. Budget 2 x 3 = 6 new tests. Delivered: 4 acceptance examples (3 driven behaviours plus 1 preserved fence, 1:1 with the authored .feature scenarios this branch can reach) and 5 unit laws. The acceptance file is the contract, the unit file is the generated law over the same behaviours, and the roadmap's own TEST PARADIGM line names both. Counting properties as one behaviour each and excluding the two preserved fences, the step sits at its budget.
